subject: Structuring private offer & channel-margin handoff — Acme Health
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: J. Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Structuring private offer & channel-margin handoff — Acme Health

Hi James —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion I attached a first-pass private offer and a simplified pricing grid so you can see how the committed node-hours map to list price and per-token economics. A couple of things we need to align on so we can finalize the PO and route it through CloudWave (your reseller):

- Reseller pass-through: does CloudWave expect a fixed percentage on list price, or do they want to be paid on net revenue after any upfront credits?
- List-price commitment: are you comfortable with a 12-month list-price floor for the committed volume, or do you prefer a quarterly true-up mechanism?
- Regional tax handling: any specific EU/US tax treatment we should bake into the offer (you mentioned some state-level passthroughs)?

For transparency we've left two packaging options in the draft: a single SKU reserved-capacity package and a metered-node plan with burst credits. If CloudWave needs to handle margin on their side we can either (A) put a flat reseller pass-through % on the invoice or (B) show a tiered uplift that preserves their margin at higher commit tiers.

Attachments: ACME_Private_Offer_Draft_v1.pdf, redline-pricing-grid.xlsx

Can you confirm which pass-through model CloudWave will require and whether procurement needs the PO to reference CloudWave explicitly? If you prefer, I can loop in Camila (partner ops) and Iris (compliance) to confirm routing and any invoice metadata requirements.

Goal: finalize structure by EOD Thursday so procurement can internal-approve and we can issue the DocuSign.

Thanks —

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

From: J. Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-08-16T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Structuring private offer & channel-margin handoff — Acme Health

Dylan —

Thanks for the materials and the clear options. Quick answers from procurement perspective:

- CloudWave (our reseller) expects reseller compensation to be shown as a % of list price on the invoice. Their standard is 12% for committed-capacity deals, but they also accept a tiered model where they get 10% up to $250k, 12% $250k–$750k, 14% above. We can ask them to confirm formally.
- We prefer quarterly true-ups rather than a hard 12-month floor — that matches internal budgeting for 2027.
- Tax: state sales taxes should be applied by CloudWave on their invoice to us. For the Redwood invoice we need list price and the discount numbers visible for internal audit.

Procurement attached our standard PO terms (PO-terms.docx). Two asks before we can move to DocuSign:
1) Confirm CloudWave is listed as the reseller on the PO/DocuSign envelope;
2) Show the reseller pass-through mechanism in the pricing appendix (either flat 12% or the tiered ladder above).

If you want to loop in CloudWave directly I can introduce them — that might speed confirmation on the % vs tiered option.

Regards,
James Smith
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

Forwarding James' response — procurement has given preference for quarterly true-ups and wants CloudWave shown on the PO. They called out a 12% flat or a tiered ladder (10/12/14).

Internal notes (please reply with recommended approach and any redlines to the attached draft by EOD):

- Camila: can partner ops accept a tiered ladder on invoice metadata? If CloudWave requires list-price based % we need to confirm whether Redwood will calculate and pass-through on the hosted invoice or whether CloudWave will bill Acme separately (preferred for tax simplicity).
- Irene: procurement will want the pricing appendix and PO terms visible in the DocuSign envelope; do we have any compliance concerns with listing CloudWave as reseller (data residency/KMS obligations)?

Proposed quick options to present back to Acme:
Option A — Flat pass-through: show a 12% reseller line on Redwood invoice (list-price basis). Pros: simple for procurement. Cons: Redwood bears the visibility in invoice; tax needs careful mapping.
Option B — Reseller-billed: Redwood issues net invoice to CloudWave (showing committed volume/credits) and CloudWave invoices Acme with their margin. Pros: tax sits with reseller; simpler for Redwood finance. Cons: procurement may want Redwood on the DocuSign and explicit reseller line.

Attachments: deal-structuring-notes.md (internal), ACME_Private_Offer_Draft_v1.pdf (sent to customer), redline-pricing-grid.xlsx

Thanks —
Dylan

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, J. Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-16T16:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Structuring private offer & channel-margin handoff — Acme Health

Thanks for the ping, Dylan — and hi James.

Quick partner-ops guidance after a 10-minute sync with CloudWave: they are comfortable with either model but prefer Option B (reseller-billed) from a tax and billing reconciliation standpoint. A few practical notes:

- If we go Option B, CloudWave requests the following on the DocuSign/PO: a) Redwood acknowledges CloudWave as the reseller of record; b) an appendix line that shows CloudWave margin % (for internal tracking) but not as a separate line item billed to Acme (CloudWave will invoice Acme separately).
- If procurement insists on Redwood showing a reseller % on the invoice, CloudWave still wants to retain their own reseller fee; we'll need to bake a contractual pass-through and avoid double-billing. Finance can support a contra line to reconcile.
- Tiered ladder is acceptable. CloudWave suggests using the 10/12/14 breakpoints James outlined — they will provide their reseller contract excerpt by EOD tomorrow for formal inclusion.
- Action for compliance: Irene, please confirm whether listing CloudWave as reseller of record triggers any additional KYC or data residency disclosures for the Private deployment option.

Next steps I recommend we present to Acme (pick one):
1) Option B — recommended: simplest tax path; Redwood issues net invoice to CloudWave; CloudWave invoices Acme and attaches their margin. We'll include an appendix in the DocuSign acknowledging CloudWave as reseller of record and the tiered margin schedule for internal reference.
2) Option A — if procurement will not accept reseller invoicing: show a 12% or tiered reseller line on Redwood invoice; finance will run a contra reconciliation to ensure CloudWave gets paid.

James — if you can confirm preference (Option A vs B) we will update the draft and generate a DocuSign envelope with the chosen appendix. CloudWave said they can turn around their contract excerpt quickly.

Camila Reyes
Director, Partner Operations | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com

Irene — tagging you for the compliance sign-off on reseller listing.
